author: Alexandra Topping Political correspondent
description:
School staff tell focus groups they believe school system in England and Wales cannot deal with attendance crisis

Teachers have so little belief in the importance of pupils’ full school attendance that they would take their own children on term time holidays if they could, staff have told a three-year research programme.

Frontline staff do not believe the school system is set up to deal with an ongoing attendance crisis in England and Wales, where nearly one in five children are now missing at least 10% of school, according to a report based on in-depth conversations with teachers.

Continue reading...
title: Teachers say holidays in term can be worth more than time in school

author: Christopher Hippensteel
description:
Cohen has not personally asked Trump for a pardon, but he submitted an application to the White House after his request was denied by the Biden administration

Donald Trump on Wednesday said he would consider pardoning Michael Cohen, the former fixer whom he once branded a “rat” for testifying against him in court and before Congress, but with whom he has recently staged a stunning public reconciliation.

Asked by a reporter whether he would grant Cohen’s appeal for presidential clemency, Trump said: “If everything is checking out, it’s something I would consider.”

Continue reading...
title: Trump says he would consider pardon for former attorney Michael Cohen

author: Guardian staff
description:
Follow the day’s news live

Don’t appease One Nation on migration, Malinauskas warns

The South Australian premier, Peter Malinauskas, has issued a stern warning for the federal government not to join the “madness” of cutting migration to appease One Nation.

Above all else, preserve our strong migration program … The correct political response to anti-immigration politics and populists is not appeasement.

More troubling is the prospect of mainstream politics entering a political race to the bottom for who can cut migration numbers the most. This is not unfortunate – this is madness.

Imagine if we did this to the mining industry, there world be an ad on every television station and mobile phone about how we’re killing the goose that lays the golden egg. It is crazy.
title: Politics live: Kevin Rudd urges more multilateral diplomacy; UK hopeful Australia will join West Bank trade ban

author: Lisa Cox
description:
Exclusive: State government delayed releasing major report into the health of the koala population for more than 12 months

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Victorian government sat on a report for more than 12 months that found the state’s koala population was in chronically poor health.

The review of the state’s koala populations, led by state science agency the Arthur Rylah Institute in conjunction with scientists from major universities, was completed for the Victorian government in June 2025.
title: Victoria’s koalas in chronically poor health and population is half what was previously estimated

author: Aamna Mohdin Community affairs correspondent
description:
Spiritual leaders stress diversity of views within Jewish community and warn against inaction on settler violence

Prominent British rabbis have backed Ed Miliband’s sanctions on Israeli settlements, warning that the time for inaction on settler violence must come to an end.

The intervention comes after the UK’s chief rabbi, the spiritual leader of mainstream Orthodox Jews in the UK, Sir Ephraim Mirvis, described UK sanctions against illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied Palestinian territories as a “dark day for British Jews” and warned they could embolden people who “use hatred as a weapon against Jews”.

Continue reading...
title: Senior UK rabbis come out in support of sanctions on Israeli settlements

author: Dara Kerr
description:
John Ternus helms his first major event as head of $4.5tn company, with a folding iPhone widely expected

John Ternus, Apple’s new CEO, helmed the company’s annual showcase of new iPhones and other products on Wednesday. It was the first time the public got a feel for the executive, who is filling the shoes of Tim Cook and his predecessor, Steve Jobs, at the $4.5tn tech giant.

The event kicked off with a video montage of characters describing the best way to start a movie, from a getaway scene to a closeup of woman revealing her true identity, before the well-known voice of Cook piped in.

Continue reading...
title: Apple’s new CEO introduces himself at annual showcase: ‘I continue to be inspired every single day’

author: Lauren Aratani
description:
Scott Bessent made announcement on Wednesday as bond yields rose to highest point since 2008 financial crisis

  • US politics live – latest updates

The US treasury will buy back $6bn worth of government debt in an effort to alleviate a sell-off in the US bond market, the treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, announced on Wednesday.

Rising inflation and uncertainty from the war in Iran have spooked investors from US bonds, what has historically been known to be one of the safest investment vehicles. Treasury yields have been rising, with the yield for the 30-year treasury bond hitting about 5.2% – the highest yield since the 2008 financial crisis.
title: US treasury to buy back $6bn in government debt to alleviate bond market

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
One researcher who resigned said many in industry believe that without regulation AI could kill off humanity

Artificial intelligence could kill off humanity within the decade, according to three researchers with the industry giant Anthropic, one of whom has quit his job in protest.

The latest doom-laden predictions came in posts on social media on Tuesday by a researcher who said he resigned because Anthropic and his previous employer, OpenAI, were ignoring or at best mishandling their response to the threat.

Continue reading...
title: Anthropic researchers say AI could cause human extinction by 2030

author: Oliver Milman
description:
Brandon Herrera of state’s 23rd congressional district calls insults against women and unhoused people ‘jokes’

A Republican candidate for a key congressional district in Texas has come under scrutiny over a series of derogatory comments made about women in his social media posts and videos.

Brandon Herrera, who is the GOP candidate for Texas’s 23rd congressional district, has made a string of insults while fashioning a rightwing online persona as the “AK Guy”, and hosts a YouTube channel with more than 4 million subscribers that tests and reviews firearms.

Continue reading...
title: Texas Republican in race for key House seat under fire for derogatory comments

author: Patrick Commins Economics editor
description:
The breakdown of the US-Iran ceasefire, rising oil prices and the explosion in data centre investment are making the central bank’s task harder

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

For five years the Reserve Bank has been trying to wrangle inflation back to its 2.5% target, and for years it has essentially failed.

The result is a cost of living crisis
title: The RBA hoped this year’s three interest rate rises would tame inflation – but nothing is going their way

author: Melissa Segura in Santa Fe
description:
Residents denounce suggestion to rename state ‘New America’, save some Republicans who insist it was ‘satire’

  • US politics live – latest updates

When scrolling through social media over the Labor Day weekend, actor, comedian and native New Mexican Steven Michael Quezada was stopped cold by a post about Donald Trump’s recent call to rename New Mexico to New America.

“At first I thought, nah, that’s got to be a joke,” said Quezada, who played drug enforcement agent Steven Gomez in the legendary TV series Breaking Bad.

Continue reading...
title: New Mexicans slam Trump’s threat to change state’s name

author: Donna Lu
description:
Climate Council forecasts more than 267,000 coastal properties will be damaged by flooding by 2100, costing hundreds of billions of dollars

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

When grazier Peter Lake moved to the Clarence Valley in the New South Wales northern rivers region in 2007, he knew was “buying in flood country with … eyes open”.

His cattle farm, about halfway between Yamba and Grafton, borders the Coldstream River and has flooded five times since 2009.

Continue reading...
title: Peter’s farm is on ‘flood country’. As Australia’s sea levels rise, safe land is vanishing and costs are huge

author: Jonathan Barrett Business editor
description:
Despite falls in some parts of the market, prices are showing signs of stabilising as investors exit and first-time buyers move in, analysts say

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

High-end homes are recording steep price falls, while more affordable properties are proving resilient, leaving Australians to experience the market downturn in very different ways, new data shows.

Upper-quartile house values in the country’s two biggest markets, Sydney and Melbourne, are now down more than 10% from their peaks, according to analysis from Cotality.

Continue reading...
title: High-end property hit by steepest price falls as affordable end of Australia’s housing market proves resilient

author: Catie McLeod Consumer affairs reporter
description:
Some rental platforms encourage hopeful tenants to share ‘excessive’ amount of information, Consumer Policy Research Centre review finds

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

So-called “RentTech” companies may be circumventing new Victorian laws designed to protect tenants’ personal data by asking for information outside the rental application process, a review as found.

The Consumer Policy Research Centre (CPRC) identified rental platforms that encouraged hopeful tenants to share an “excessive” amount of personal information, or asked them questions that were “completely outside” the new rules.
title: RentTech companies still asking tenants for personal details ‘completely outside’ new Victorian laws

author: Guardian staff and agency
description:
Downed trees cause widespread power outages on Kauai as winds and rains rip up roads and coat homes in mud

Damaging winds and heavy rains from Hurricane Lowell caused significant damage on Hawaii’s western islands, knocking out power to thousands, ripping up stretches of road and drenching homes and stores with mud.

Fierce winds downed trees and caused widespread power outages on the island of Kauai, home to 73,000 residents. The Kauai Island Utility Cooperative reported that nearly all of its roughly 35,000 members were without power on Tuesday.

Continue reading...
title: Western Hawaii islands survey damage after Hurricane Lowell passes by

author: Oliver Milman and agencies
description:
TSA PreCheck program members will be eligible to send off friends and family at gate in change to post-9/11 rule

  • Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email

Some people without plane tickets will be allowed to pass through security at US airports and go to gates to see off family or friends, rolling back a rule that was introduced after the 9/11 terrorist attacks.

Certain people who are part of the TSA PreCheck program but who do not have tickets to fly will be able to go through security to airport gates, the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) said.

Continue reading
title: US airports to let some people without tickets pass through security

author: Martin Belam
description:
The state can’t use new congressional districts under one court order – or its old ones under another. Plus, the architects in Europe turning urban spaces into areas of climate respite

  • Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here

Good morning. Clashing court rulings plunged Missouri’s congressional elections into uncertainty less than two months before the November midterms that will decide which party controls a closely divided Congress.

Conservative justice Brett Kavanaugh denied the emergency request from Missouri officials to use a congressional map in November that was redrawn with Donald Trump’s support to give Republicans an edge in the midterms, but a ruling by a federal judge in Misso
title: Conflicting court rulings on Missouri map threaten November’s election | First Thing

author: Michael Sainato
description:
AFL-CIO calls for ban on such labels to protect consumers and workers from surveillance pricing and job cuts

The universal adoption of electronic shelf labels in grocery stores across the US could cost tens of thousands of jobs and billions of dollars in lost wages while further driving up grocery costs, according to a report released on Tuesday.

An analysis by the AFL-CIO Tech Institute of the label manufacturers’ own marketing materials found the universal adoption of electronic shelf labels, which are marketed to retailers as a cost-cutting measure, could cost workers between $1.6bn to $6.9bn in lost wages annually and affect between 44,223 and 191,633 jobs.

Continue reading...
title: Electronic shelf labels likely to cost jobs and drive up grocery prices, US report warns

author: Tom Ambrose
description:
President to give speeches on both days of unprecedented gathering

  • Republican midterm convention will be ‘Trumpist pageantry’ – at the party’s own risk

  • Sign up for US Breaking News email

Donald Trump gave sizable holiday gifts to four White House aides, according to new financial disclosures released by the administration, including $45,000 to executive assistant Natalie Harp.

Communications adviser Margo Martin and deputy director of Oval Office operations Chamberlain Harris also received $45,000, while director of Oval Office operations Walt N
title: Trump center stage at RNC in midterms gamble – US politics live

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
Kent Blacklidge, who officials say was ‘directly involved with child exploitation cases’, turned himself in last week

A federal law enforcement agent tasked with “trying to provide justice in cases involving kids” has been charged with child rape in Alabama, state authorities said on Tuesday.

Kent Blacklidge, described as a special agent with Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), turned himself over to the Baldwin county jail on 5 September in connection with a grand jury indictment charging him with first- and second-degree rape, sodomy and sexual abuse, police in the city of Spanish Fort said in a statement.

Continue reading...
title: Homeland security agent charged with child rape in Alabama, officials say

author: Adam Gabbatt
description:
Republicans plan to center the US president at the two-day event, while slamming Democrats as socialists

Republicans will gather in Texas on Wednesday for a rare “midterm convention”, as they attempt to convince Americans to vote for a party led by a deeply unpopular president who has overseen price increases, inflation, and led the US into an increasingly unpopular war.

Donald Trump will dominate the two-day convention, appearing both nights as the GOP works to cling to control of the House of Representatives in November. Republicans plan to put the president at the center of the event, a bold strategy given his approval rating is hovering at about 38%, while accusing the Democratic party as being socialist and out of touch with Americans.

Continue reading
title: Republicans in fight to hold on to majority look to ‘midterm convention’ to overcome Trump unpopularity

author: Aletha Adu Political correspondent
description:
Foreign secretary says Sir Ephraim Mirvis wrong to suggest measures against Israeli settlements will make British Jews less safe

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Ed Miliband has rejected warnings from the UK’s chief rabbi that the government’s sanctions against illegal Israeli settlements will make British Jews less safe, as he stressed ministers can confront the actions of Benjamin Netanyahu’s government while also fighting antisemitism.

The foreign secretary announced sweeping sanctions on trade with Israeli settlements in the West Bank on Tuesday, with the government taking the position that Israel’s occupation of the Palestinian territory was unlawful.

An impo
title: Miliband rejects chief rabbi’s claim that West Bank sanctions put UK Jews at risk

author: Adeshola Ore
description:
NSW police say a vehicle was seen driving away from the scene in Punchbowl in the city’s south-west

A man has been shot dead in a carpark of a Sydney community centre in the city’s south-west.

Emergency services were called to the community centre on Rossmore Avenue, in Punchbowl on Wednesday evening, following reports of a shooting.

Continue reading...
title: Man shot dead in Sydney community centre carpark

author: Mark Sweney
description:
New roles at Woking-based manufacturer will include positions for indirect and agency workers

The British supercar manufacturer McLaren is to create 1,000 jobs in a welcome boost to the UK’s struggling automotive industry.

The carmaker is creating the jobs as part of a £450m investment in its technology centre in Woking, near to the plant where it manufactures all of its vehicles.

Continue reading...
title: Supercar maker McLaren to create 1,000 UK jobs as part of £450m tech investment

author: Luca Ittimani
description:
Funding from $560m invitation-only scheme prompts calls to make grant rules more transparent

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Anthony Albanese has claimed he did not know he was a member of his local golf club when his government gave it $6m for renovations, accusing the ABC of inappropriate reporting.

The money came from an opaque $560m invitation-only grants scheme to fund projects Labor promised at the 2025 election, largely for Labor-held seats, prompting calls to make grant rules more transparent.

Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics
title: Albanese says ABC ‘should do better’ after it revealed his membership of golf club given $6m grant

author: Mark Sweney
description:
Martin Rolfe, who faces pressure to resign, due to brief Heidi Alexander after cancellations pass 1,900

  • Business live – latest updates

The boss of the air traffic control provider Nats has been summoned to meet the UK transport secretary as the number of flight cancellations passed 1,900 in a second day of disruption for hundreds of thousands of passengers.

Martin Rolfe, who is facing increasing pressure to resign over a third major stoppage to flights in just over three years, is due to brief Heidi Alexander on Wednesday.

Continue re
title: Nats boss summoned by UK transport secretary as flight chaos enters second day

author: Lauren Almeida
description:
Brent crude up by more than 2% after latest fire between US and Iran in Gulf and Houthi attacks on Saudi cities

  • Business live – latest updates

The price of oil has risen above $100 a barrel for the first time since July as the escalating conflict in the Middle East threatens further disruption to global supplies.

Brent crude, the international benchmark for oil prices, rose 2.1% past the milestone after tensions stepped up in the Gulf amid the latest tit-for-tat exchange of fire between the US and Iran.

Continue reading...
title: Oil prices rise above $100 a barrel for first time since July as Iran war escalates

author: Luca Ittimani
description:
White House warns trading partners against ‘imposing digital services taxes, fines, and other forms of extortion’ on US tech sector

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

The Trump administration will confront Australia over its plan to force digital platforms to take down harmful content and let users opt out of algorithm-generated “for you” feeds.

Big tech companies would be fined more than $100m for breaching the proposed laws and the Australian government is under pressure to raise those fines eve
title: Trump administration to confront Australia over Labor’s social media algorithm plan

author: Sarah Basford Canales
description:
The former National Socialist Network is challenging ban in high court, arguing law breaches implied freedom of political communication

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

The White Australia party is a “modern manifestation” of Adolf Hitler’s Nazi movement and would motivate hate crimes against sections of the country, the high court has heard.

The White Australia party, formerly known as the National Socialist Network (NSN), was
title: White Australia party is ‘modern manifestation’ of Nazi movement and should be banned, commonwealth tells high court

author: Amanda Meade
description:
Downing Centre court hears that the alleged victim was usually outgoing but his demeanour changed at a meeting with Jones at his apartment

• Listen to the podcast Alan Jones on Trial

A politician who worked with an alleged victim of Alan Jones has told a Sydney court the man looked uncharacteristically “sunken and diminished” when meeting with the broadcaster at his Circular Quay apartment.

The former MP, who Guardian Australia has chosen not to name because it may lead to the identification of the alleged victim, known as complainant C, said the man was usually outgoing and engaged but his demeanour changed once he sat down at a table with his former boss.

Continue reading...
title: Alleged victim of Alan Jones looked ‘sunken and diminished’, politician tells court

author: Matthew Taylor and Pippa Neill
description:
Green leader says ministers must stop ‘hiding the truth’ about threat to UK security from climate and nature crisis

Zack Polanski will challenge Andy Burnham’s government to publish an unredacted version of an explosive report by the UK’s spy chiefs that found the collapse of overseas ecosystems would have catastrophic consequences for the UK’s national security.

The Green party leader in England will demand that the prime minister come clean about the scale and impact of the climate and nature crisis and call on the government to publish in full the report that warns the UK faces devastating security consequences.

Continue reading...
title: Polanski calls for report on ecosystem collapse to be published in full

author: Krishani Dhanji and Tom McIlroy
description:
The Canning MP says the cartoon, first posted by Hanson on social media over a month ago, calls him a traitor eight times

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Liberal frontbencher and SAS veteran Andrew Hastie has called Pauline Hanson and Barnaby Joyce “lying cowards”, after he claimed a One Nation cartoon portrayed him as a traitor for providing evidence in court against Ben Roberts-Smith.

Hastie further escalated his fight with One Nation on Wednesday, a day after the Canning MP used a letter to
title: Andrew Hastie accuses Pauline Hanson and Barnaby Joyce of being ‘lying cowards’ over One Nation ‘traitor’ cartoon

author: Hettie O'Brien
description:
In today’s newsletter: Ed Miliband has announced the strongest statement on Israel’s actions ever issued by the the UK government, but will it make a meaningful difference to Palestinians?

Good morning. For almost half a century, British governments have condemned illegal Israeli settlements, acknowledging they represent an obstacle to peace and threaten the prospect of a two-state solution. And yet no government has ever compelled Israel to stop its expansion.

Ed Miliband’s statement in the House of Commons yesterday was an attempt to change that. In a powerful and emotive speech, the foreign secretary recounted childhood memories of picking oranges on his grandmother’s kibbutz, accused Israeli “terrorists” of ethnic cleansing in the West Bank and announced a series of new measures intended to address what he described as a “deeply painful contrast” between rhetoric and reality.

UK news | Police have been told by the government
title: Wednesday briefing: Inside sweeping UK sanctions on trade with Israeli settlements

author: Alexandra Topping Political correspondent
description:
Key thinkers suggest other radical measures in Compass report such as free personal social care and abolishing Lords

Andy Burnham should tackle inequality in the UK by introducing a wealth tax, universal free personal social care and bringing gas and electricity networks under public ownership, according to a report from more than a dozen influential thinkers.

In the lead-up to the first budget of the chancellor, John Healey, this autumn, the Compass thinktank has collated 70 policy options from 15 leftwing thinkers that they argue would deliver on the prime minister’s promise to end 40 years of neoliberalism.

Continue reading...
title: Burnham urged to tackle inequality with policies including wealth tax

author: Jon Henley Europe correspondent
description:
A continent-wide crisis of confidence is creating fertile ground for far-right narratives of decline, report suggests

Europeans overwhelmingly want a strong, united and independent Europe but question whether it can get there, according to a study that suggests a continent-wide crisis of confidence is creating fertile ground for far-right narratives of decline.

The report, based on 5,800 interviews in France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Poland and the UK and analysis of the way Europe is discussed in the politics and media of 15 countries, paints a picture of an ambitious but disillusioned public.

Continue reading...
title: Europeans want a united Europe but question whether it can get there, study finds

author: Penry Buckley
description:
Jeremy Greenwood tells inquiry note contained agreement with Jean Nassif as counsel assisting says ‘threads of your story pull apart very quickly’

A Liberal operative has denied making up a “pink” or “fuchsia”-coloured piece of paper which he says was the record of an agreement with a property developer worth up to $5m, a corruption inquiry has heard.

Jeremy Greenwood told the Independent Commission Against Corruption (Icac) on Wednesday that the note, which he did not mention in a preliminary interview with the watchdog, was not a “recent invention”.

Continue reading...
title: Liberal operative denies he invented pink paper record of agreement with fugitive developer, Icac hears

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
Roni Carlson, in wake of mistrial, says holdout juror could not be persuaded while colleague calls him ‘very arrogant’

A lone juror in the trial of Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts mother accused of the murder of her three children, would not agree to acquit Clancy despite expressing reasonable doubt about whether she was guilty, the jury’s foreperson said in an interview airing Monday.

Speaking to NBC 10 Boston just days after Clancy’s trial ended in a mistrial, Roni Carlson, the foreperson, confirmed there was one holdout juror who would not be persuaded to acquit Clancy due to insanity.

In the US, call the national maternal health hotline on 1-833-852-626
title: Lindsay Clancy juror had reasonable doubt but would not agree to acquit, foreperson says

author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
description:
Penny Wong has concerns about blanket ban announced by UK, France and Canada, but says new ‘targeted measures’ planned over Israeli settlers

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia is preparing another round of sanctions against Israel but has stopped short of joining the UK in banning trade with Israeli settlements in the West Bank.

Overnight, the UK government offered its
title: Australia considers new Israel sanctions but won’t join UK in banning trade with ‘settler terrorists’

author: Josh Taylor Technology reporter
description:
Exclusive: The Australian Criminal Intelligence Commission, which has access to NDIA data, used Palantir as part of a multi-agency fraud taskforce

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Personal information of national disability insurance scheme participants may have ended up in controversial software company Palantir’s analytics platform as part of a massive multi-agency sharing program investigating fraud, Guardian Australia can reveal.

There have been calls to ban the use of Palantir’s software by the Australian government since May, after it implied some cultures are inferior to others i
title: NDIS data may have ended up in Palantir’s analytics platform as part of efforts to curb fraud

author: Victoria Bekiempis
description:
The documents are available through an online portal that was launched three days before the 25th anniversary of September 11

New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani’s administration has released more than 170,000 pages of municipal records involving the impact of the September 11 attacks on air quality health, as well as the city’s response.

Mamdani announced the documents and an online portal for accessing them on Tuesday. The release comes alongside the settlement of two lawsuits pursued by 9/11 Health Watch, which fought for access to these long-withheld documents.

Continue reading...
title: Mamdani releases 170,000 pages of records regarding impact on air quality of the 9/11 attacks

author: Shrai Popat
description:
Frontrunner Sununu beats Scott Brown to earn Republican nod in closely watched race in November

Former senator John E Sununu triumphed on Tuesday in the New Hampshire Republican Senate primary Scott Brown, earning the GOP nod in what will likely be a must-win race if Democrats hope to seize the upper chamber.

Sununu, 61, was the clear frontrunner in the GOP primary. He served one term in the Senate from 2003 to 2009.

Continue reading...
title: Trump-backed John Sununu wins New Hampshire Republican Senate primary

author: Shrai Popat
description:
Pappas fends off challenge from progressive Karishma Manzur in seat to be vacated by retiring Jeanne Shaheen

Congressman Chris Pappas beat back progressive challenger Karishma Manzur in the Democratic primary for US Senate on Tuesday, advancing as most observers expected to what will be a closely watched general election that is critical to Democratic hopes of flipping the upper chamber.

The two were competing for the nomination that opened up after Jeanne Shaheen, 79, the state’s three‑term incumbent Democratic senator, announced her retirement.

Continue reading...
title: Congressman Chris Pappas wins New Hampshire Democratic Senate primary

author: Agence France-Presse
description:
The affluent city-state has justified high-end salaries for its political leaders, arguing they attract talent and ensure good governance

Singapore’s prime minister has been given a $1m pay rise as the affluent city-state announced a dramatic one-off salary boost for government ministers.

The pay increases add more than 60% to what are already the world’s highest ministerial salaries.

Continue reading...
title: Singapore boosts PM’s salary by $1m amid major pay rise for ministers
